paper_metadata.title: Outcomes of newly diagnosed idiopathic generalized epilepsy syndromes in a non-pediatric setting

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses a well-defined sampling frame (First Seizure Clinic) with clear inclusion/exclusion criteria and describes the baseline characteristics of the IGES cohort in detail. The recruitment period is long (20 years), and the setting is clearly defined.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Adolescent and adult patients with suspected seizure disorders were referred to a specialist first seizure service by general practitioners, accident and emergency physicians and other clinicians.
items.reasoning: The source population is clearly defined as adolescent and adult patients referred to a specific regional specialist service.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: A total of 890 patients were diagnosed with epilepsy after presenting to the First Seizure Clinic at the Epilepsy Unit in the Western Infirmary in Glasgow, between August 1981 and May 2001.
items.reasoning: The sampling frame is a specific clinic over a 20-year period, capturing consecutive diagnoses.

items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).

items.evidence_snippet: Logistic regression analysis was used to ascertain the influence of various risk factors... In a univariate logistic regression analysis, a history of febrile seizures was the only factor associated with a significantly lower remission rate
items.reasoning: The authors mention logistic regression but only report univariate results in the main findings. It is unclear if a multivariable model was successfully fitted or if it was abandoned due to the small sample size (n=103).

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The analysis is straightforward, but the small sample size for specific syndromes (e.g., Childhood Absence Epilepsy n=2) limits the power of the statistical tests. There is a risk of over-interpreting the univariate finding for febrile seizures without multivariable adjustment.
